items.headline: European Commission proposes a Quantum Act and a 50 billion euro tech fund
items.what: The European Commission proposed a Quantum Act on Wednesday, a draft law meant to turn European quantum research into products and services, strengthen supply chains and prepare digital systems for post-quantum cryptography. The proposal also lays the groundwork for a Sovereign Tech Equity Fund, which the Commission says would provide equity financing for technologies central to European tech independence. EU tech chief Henna Virkkunen said officials are targeting 50 billion euros for the fund. The draft law still needs agreement from EU member states and the European Parliament before it can become law.
items.why: Europe trails the United States and China in AI, chips and cloud computing, and the proposal is the bloc's main move to close that gap in quantum technology. The fund would be one of the largest public tech investment vehicles in Europe, and the procurement rules would favour European companies.

items.headline: US proposes new tariffs on 14 trading partners, with China facing 20 percent
items.what: The US Trade Representative proposed new tariffs on goods from 14 trading partners, including China, the European Union, India and Japan, after an eight month investigation into excess industrial capacity. China would face a proposed 20 percent duty on top of roughly 25 percent tariffs from the first Trump term, while the European Union would start at 15 percent. The proposal covers steel, aluminium, electric vehicles, appliances, solar products and other goods. It will go through a public comment period and a hearing before it can take effect, which officials said could push implementation into January. The move follows the Supreme Court striking down the administration's earlier sweeping tariffs in February.
items.why: The technology angle is in the goods themselves: the proposal names electric vehicles and solar products among the products Washington says are flooding world markets, and the partner list includes Taiwan, South Korea and Japan, the centre of the chip supply chain, though neither source says semiconductors are themselves in scope. US technology shares took the early hit, with the tech heavy Nasdaq down 0.6 percent at the close after falling more than 4 percent in early trading. The duties are proposed, not final: a public comment period and a hearing come first.

items.headline: GitHub recovers from database fault that disrupted Issues, pull requests and Actions
items.what: GitHub reported degraded service across its core products on Wednesday after high database load caused increased failures. Issues and pull requests were unavailable for a time, while Actions, Git operations, Packages, Pages, webhooks and API requests ran with degraded performance. GitHub said it rebalanced database load and began seeing recovery within about half an hour, and reported the degradation mitigated within the hour.
items.why: GitHub hosts code and collaboration workflows for millions of developers, so a fault across its core services stalls software work worldwide until it is fixed.

items.headline: FCC authorizes SpaceX to deploy one million satellites for data centers in space
items.what: The US Federal Communications Commission authorized SpaceX to deploy up to one million orbital compute modules, known as the Starmind constellation, to process data in orbit for use on Earth. The agency called it the first authorization of its kind in the United States and said the system would help meet growing demand for AI computing. The modules would run on solar power. Under the license, SpaceX must begin deployment by November 2033, deploy 100,000 modules by November 2035 and half the constellation by November 2038.
items.why: Orbital data centers would move large scale computing off the ground for the first time, and the approval sets the terms for a new class of space infrastructure aimed at AI workloads.

items.headline: 1Password discloses breach of customer account records after employee GitHub account compromise
items.what: 1Password said an attacker gained access to an employee's corporate GitHub account and used it to reach private source code repositories and push malicious code to backend services. The code downloaded account records for a subset of users, including names and email addresses, account and user identifiers, account creation and last sign in times, public keys, Secure Remote Password protocol parameters, and tokens embedded in emailed links for invitations, provisioning and account recovery. The attacker also copied source code and reached the company's continuous integration and delivery system. 1Password said customer vault contents and the keys that protect them were not accessed at any point, and that it does not store account passwords or Secret Keys. The company disabled the compromised GitHub account, revoked the stolen token, rotated or revoked credentials that may have been exposed, and lengthened the codes in invitation and recovery emails from six numeric digits to ten alphanumeric characters. It said it found no evidence of account takeovers and has hired independent cybersecurity experts to validate its remediation.
items.why: 1Password is one of the most widely used password managers, so a breach of its backend systems matters even though vault contents stayed out of reach. The stolen names and email addresses give attackers a verified list of 1Password users to target with phishing, and the company warns customers to expect fake invitations and account recovery messages. The incident also shows how a single compromised employee account can become a route into production systems.

items.headline: OpenAI fixes GPT-6.2 billing error that had discounted usage for paid users
items.what: OpenAI said a billing error at the launch of GPT-6.2 on November 17 had undercounted usage of GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol for most subscribers. With the fix in place, the same work uses up a plan allowance faster: users reach their limits about 40 percent faster on Astra and 25 percent faster on Sol than last week. OpenAI said other models are unaffected, it will not charge for the undercounted past usage, and users on Go, Plus, Pro and Business plans will get one banked usage reset. From December, ChatGPT and Codex will also share one usage allowance for those plans.
items.why: GPT-6.2 Astra is OpenAI's flagship model and Sol is its everyday model, so the correction changes how much work paying subscribers get from their plans. It lands days before the shared ChatGPT and Codex allowance takes effect, which puts chat and coding usage into one pool.

items.headline: Equal1, NVIDIA and Dell demonstrate hybrid quantum and classical computing in one server rack
items.what: Equal1, NVIDIA and Dell demonstrated a hybrid quantum and classical computing setup at the SC26 supercomputing conference in Chicago. Equal1's rack-mounted RacQ silicon quantum computer, which draws 1.6 kilowatts, ran alongside Dell data centre servers inside a standard rack. NVIDIA NVQLink provided low-latency communication between the quantum processor and graphics processors, with automated gate tuning from NVIDIA's open Ising Calibration models, and Dell's Quantum Intelligent Orchestrator software coordinated work across the classical and quantum hardware.
items.why: Quantum computers have mostly run as standalone machines, so fitting one into a standard data centre rack with live links to classical servers is a step toward running quantum and classical work together in production settings. The demonstration also shows the three vendors' software working as one system, from gate tuning to job orchestration.
